semantic_contract: cdecl free function, two UTF-16 file-name arguments, no return value, SEH-framed. Argument 1 is the temporary source name and argument 2 is the final destination name. Invariants, in the order the body performs them: (1) resolve the Resource::SaveAreaID::GamesGame0 service and read its directory path through virtual slot +0x28; (2) deep-copy that path into a local 16-bit string; (3) call the delete-tree port on that copy and discard the result, so whatever is at the save-area path is removed before anything is installed; (4) build dest = base + dest_name; (5) build src = base + source_name; (6) build backup = dest + ".old"; (7) if dest exists as a regular file, move dest to backup with MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING | MOVEFILE_COPY_ALLOWED; (8) unconditionally move src to dest with the same flags, ignoring the result entirely; (9) if backup exists, delete it with DeleteFileW; (10) release all eight string buffers, freeing a buffer only when its masked byte span exceeds 2 and the pointer is non-null. The net effect is a temp-file promotion with a transient one-step rollback copy: the previous contents of dest survive a failed promotion only for the duration of the call, and both failure paths are silent because no return value is tested.
classification_rationale: Every one of the 239 instructions is read, all eleven callees are resolved to their operations from their own decompiled bodies, all constants and literals are verified by live reads, the two caller arguments are read as literal strings, the base directory id matches an SDK enum value exactly, and the file-operation semantics are proven from GetFileAttributesW / MoveFileExW / DeleteFileW inside the callees rather than assumed. It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC because of one specific unresolved mechanical point rather than a naming gap: the delete-tree port at 0x00689286 is provably called with a NUL-terminated copy of the base directory path, and a recursive delete of the Game0 save directory immediately before moving a file into a subdirectory of that same directory is self-contradictory unless the port's directory branch does not actually remove the directory or the returned path is a file rather than a folder. The evidence fixes what the call is, not why it is there, so the function's purpose is bounded rather than fully determined.
semantic_findings: The routine is a save-file promotion: temp name -> final name, with a ".old" copy used only to keep the previous contents recoverable across the move and deleted before returning.

The three paths are built by plain concatenation with no separator, so the base path returned by the save area must already be separator-terminated; this is a constraint on the unseen getter, not something the body establishes.

The existence test and the DeleteFileW are both guarded, but the promotion move is not, and no return value is examined anywhere. A missing source file therefore leaves the destination removed with no error reported to the caller.

Ghidra's name IO_File_Remove for 0x00931fa0 is wrong: its body is GetFileAttributesW plus a not-a-directory test, i.e. a file-existence predicate. Recording this because the name would otherwise invert the two guarded branches.

The MOVE flags are the literal 3, i.e. MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING | MOVEFILE_COPY_ALLOWED, and the overwrite argument is the literal 1 at both call sites, which disables the callee's own destination-exists bail-out. The rotation therefore overwrites a stale .old unconditionally.
The string type is a three-pointer UTF-16 buffer with a byte-valued capacity, and the NUL store at 0x0068927a is a 16-bit store, which fixes the element size at 2 bytes independently of the host ABI.

All four call sites are in unrelated subsystems (the editor region, the user-data/boot region and two others) and all pass their names as caller stack buffers, so this is a shared file utility rather than an editor-specific one. The briefing's Editor subsystem label is a clustering artefact.
The function is not a vtable entry anywhere Ghidra has typed, and no DATA reference points at it.
unresolved_questions: Why is a recursive delete issued on the save-area base path at 0x00689286, before any file is moved into it? The argument is proven to be that path, but the intent is not recoverable from the binary. Either the path returned by slot +0x28 is a file rather than a directory, or the delete is intended to clear a stale folder whose recreation is handled elsewhere, or the call is dead in the shipping build because its result is discarded.
What does virtual slot +0x28 on the save area return, and does it end with a path separator? The receiver is constructed at runtime so no string was read.
What is 0x00932960, the routine 0x00932ae0 delegates to for a non-directory path? Not decompiled in this pass.
What is the original function name and owning class? Nothing in the binary or the SDK names it.
Why are the two exists/delete branches guarded while the promotion is not? The asymmetry may be deliberate (best-effort cleanup) or an oversight; the binary does not say.
Do the callers at 0x00580dc9 and 0x00b293d4 pass names with an embedded separator, given that the concatenation inserts none? Their arguments are stack buffers whose contents were not read.
Is the promote-and-delete sequence ever observed to run with a destination that does not exist, i.e. is the first-time-install path exercised? Static analysis cannot tell.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists for this function. A differential trace must record the string returned by the save-area virtual slot +0x28, since the whole path algebra depends on whether it is separator-terminated.
A trace must record the return value and the observable effect of 0x00932ae0 on the base path, which is the only way to resolve whether the leading delete is live behaviour or a no-op.
A trace must record whether MoveFileExW at 0x00689406 succeeds in practice, because the body discards the result and static analysis cannot predict the filesystem state.

validation.modelling_note: The reconstruction uses char16_t rather than the host wchar_t. On Windows x86-32 wchar_t is 2 bytes, and every length in this function is a byte computation over that element; using the host 4-byte wchar_t silently halves every count. This was caught by the model test and is recorded so the choice is not mistaken for a stylistic one.
